instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Lost in the Process
cards.instruction: Hide your role in the problem by distributing blame across steps, policies, and unnamed procedures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel was lost between reception and dispatch. Use the incident format I taught you; put the failed stage in the first box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left it on the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've identified transport. Write 'dispatch transferred without a receipt'. You used to skip the handover stage entirely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both departments are you. Call the bus company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll call. You finish the report: dispatch, transport, receipt control. Three stages to investigate; don't squeeze them into one name after all that training.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The birthday invitations failed address verification. Get out the checklist I taught you to use; we need to mark the stage that let us down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wrote our old address on every invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well spotted. The archive supplied an outdated location and verification missed it. Two headings, please; you used to put everything under 'mistake'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You keep the address book and posted them. Who's calling the guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do notifications. Add that third heading, and put 'insufficient staffing' across all three. No names in the headings, remember.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Outside the Scope
cards.instruction: Redirect personal or dangerous questions by declaring them irrelevant, premature, or assigned to another process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whether I broke the window isn't on this repair agenda. I taught you to chair one subject at a time; read the heading before asking me that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let's have a responsibility meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A much clearer heading than you used to write. After the repairs; we need somewhere safe to hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can meet outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the venue change through planning first. You always moved the chairs before we agreed where they went; let's settle the location.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the children the trip's postponed for bus repairs. Use the calm opening I taught you; they'll worry about Mr Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's fine. His parked bus rolled into the pond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you started with him being fine. Stop there, then say the bus needs repairs. You used to lead with the splashiest detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The parents will ask if he was driving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then everybody says, 'The parked bus needs repairs; Mr Patel is fine.' Give the office that exact line too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grandad's embarrassed about the gazebo. Tell people the garden's unavailable and we're celebrating indoors. Keep it short, the way I taught you for family speeches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's already told Aunt Jean he set it on fire.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say, 'Everyone's fine; we're celebrating indoors.' Good, you checked what she knows before giving her another version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants him to explain the fire in his birthday speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give him that same opening, then cue him to thank her for the trifle. You used to need me to steer you past a bad first story; do that for him.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: For the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to state exactly what they did, knew, or authorized before you reveal your own involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I show you the fireworks invoice, state exactly what you approved. I taught you to give a brief someone can follow, not just wave at the sky.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you buy the enormous rocket?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your wording first. Did 'make it memorable' include rockets? You used to skip the nouns when I asked for a brief.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sparklers. Nothing that needed a trailer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Much more precise. When did you tell me the trailer limit? Put that date down before I show you the delivery date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I show you my dinner invitations, who did you tell your sister she could bring? I taught you to write full names, not leave people guessing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A date. Did you invite my ex?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did you name anyone she couldn't bring? You used to expect everyone to know who you meant. My list comes after your answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My ex. I sent both of you the same message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you finally put it in writing. What time did you send it to me? We'll put that beside my invitation's time before I open the list.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Successful Compliance
cards.instruction: Describe a failed outcome as proof that the correct process was followed and therefore the system worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding cake collapsed, but your final inspection caught it. You finally used the checkpoint I taught you; the system worked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing to serve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. No defective cake reached a guest. You used to wave things through because people were waiting; today you followed the process.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The couple want a refund for the entire cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they agree with your inspection: reject the whole cake. Put 'full customer agreement' in the box I showed you. That's a complete result, for once.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Seventeen evacuation instructions, all followed. You finally remembered the route I taught you without asking me at every door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're locked in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the designated assembly point, with nobody wandering off. You used to lose half the group before the count; this is much better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't reach the handle with all twelve of us in here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All twelve accounted for, and nobody can leave before you finish. Mark both checks passed, the way I showed you. You've never kept a group together so well.
